title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
oneLinerQuestion: Find the length of the longest substring containing the same character after replacing at most k letters.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Longest Repeating Character Replacement problem asks for the length of the longest contiguous substring containing identical letters that can be formed by replacing at most k characters. Checking all possible substrings takes O(N^2) or O(N^3) time. We optimize this to linear time using a sliding window. Within any valid window `[L, R]`, the total number of characters is `windowLen = R - L + 1`. If we preserve the most frequent character in that window (occurring `maxF` times), the minimum number of replacements needed to make all characters identical is `windowLen - maxF`. As long as `windowLen - maxF <= k`, the window is valid and can be expanded. If `windowLen - maxF > k`, the required substitutions exceed our budget `k`, so we shrink the window by shifting the left boundary `L` forward until the invariant holds.

- Step 1: State Tracking & Window Initialization — We initialize a frequency hash map (or fixed-size array of 26 integers) `count = new Map()`, two boundary pointers `left = 0` and `right = 0`, a variable `maxF = 0` to track the maximum frequency of any single character seen in the current window, and `maxLength = 0` to record the global maximum length.

- Step 2: Expanding Window (Right Boundary Sweep) — We iterate through string `s` using pointer `right` from `0` to `s.length - 1`. At each step, we increment the count of `s[right]` in our frequency map: `count.set(s[right], (count.get(s[right]) || 0) + 1)`.

- Step 3: Updating Maximum Frequency (`maxF`) — We update our peak frequency: `maxF = Math.max(maxF, count.get(s[right]))`. Notably, `maxF` does not strictly need to decrease when the window shrinks, because a window can only set a new record `maxLength` if it encounters a `maxF` strictly greater than any previously recorded.

- Step 4: Window Invariant Evaluation & Contraction — We verify if the current window requires more replacements than allowed: `while ((right - left + 1) - maxF > k)`. If true, the window is invalid; we decrement the frequency of `s[left]` via `count.set(s[left], count.get(s[left]) - 1)` and contract the window from the left by incrementing `left++`.

- Step 5: Updating Global Result — Once the window is guaranteed to be valid (`(right - left + 1) - maxF <= k`), we update our longest valid window length: `maxLength = Math.max(maxLength, right - left + 1)`.

- Step 6: Termination & Return — After `right` reaches the end of string `s`, `maxLength` holds the length of the longest valid substring achievable with at most k replacements, which we return.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N) where N is the length of string `s`, as each pointer (`left` and `right`) advances from 0 to N at most once. Space Complexity: O(1) auxiliary space (or bounded O(26)) when restricted to uppercase English letters, as the frequency table stores at most 26 character counts.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION characterReplacement(s, k):
    count = EMPTY_MAP(), l = 0, maxF = 0, res = 0
    FOR r FROM 0 TO LENGTH(s) - 1 DO:
        count[s[r]] = count[s[r]] + 1
        maxF = MAX(maxF, count[s[r]])
        WHILE (r - l + 1) - maxF > k DO:
            count[s[l]] = count[s[l]] - 1; l = l + 1
        END WHILE
        res = MAX(res, r - l + 1)
    END FOR
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION
